newsitem.title: GERMANY: DT to set IPO price range on Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: DT to set IPO price range on Oct 21.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG (DT), the German telecommunications giant that will launch Europe's largest-ever share listing next month, said on Thursday it will publish the bidding range for the offering on October 21.

Earlier DT had said it would set the price range on October 22, but it has now moved the date forward to coincide with release of its final investment prospectus, which will be published in the United States on Monday.
The company also plans to provide details at a news conference on Tuesday about the stock purchase incentives it plans to offer private investors.

Analysts from the leading syndicate banks managing DT's listing expect expect a price range of between 25 marks and 30 marks. Shares will begin trading in Germany and New York on November 18 and a day later in Tokyo.

According to reports in the German press, there has been a row between DT and the main banks in charge of the listing -- Deutsche Bank AG, Dresdner Bank AG and Goldman Sachs -- over the price range and recommended share price.

Deutsche Bank reportedly angered DT by proposing a price range of between 20 marks and 30 marks. DT had hoped to earn 15 billion marks from the issue, based on 500 million shares at a price of 30 marks per share.
Neither DT nor any of the banks would comment on the reports. According to banking sources, an IPO price of around 28 marks per share now seems likely.
Announcement of the price range and publication of the final sales prospectus kick off the subscription period for the bookbuilding process by which DT will sell shares to institutional investors.
During the subscription period from October 22 to November 14, prospective investors will place tentative orders with DT, allowing the company to establish a list of investors.
DT will hold a news conference on Monday, October 21, in its Bonn offices to discuss the final sales prospectus, which will include the price range for the listing.
Then, on October 22, it will hold another news conference in Frankfurt to kick off the roadshows and the beginning of the bookbuilding process and outline purchase incentives for private investors.
